chapter: Small band, Charlie Parker and the big band
title: Changing the band: Hadnot, Gene Ramey and Countess Johnson
summary: On Bales's advice he changed trumpet and drummer; Hadnot left for St. Louis, Gene Ramey joined from Countess Johnson's group, and McShann sizes up her playing.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Actually -- let me see, there was Pete -- Pete was born in Muskogee, but he spent most time in Kansas City, you know, spent more time, you know, and -- but anyway, that was the first group that I took out and so then, you know, Walter Bales and we'd sit and talk and he says, "Well, I'll tell you what. I think you're going to have to make some changes. If I were you, I'd get a different guy on the trumpet," you know what I

mean, and he says, "Sounds like the drummer seems to be slowing the tempo down," you know what I mean. He says, "Now, I don't know nothing about this. So you just use your own judgment. I'm just --" we're setting talking, you know. He said, "But I'd like to see you get a good group." So I told him, "Well, everytime I make a change and make a better change, that's what I'll do."
So then I got Gus, [Johnson] Had not was supposed to have went with me on bass instead of Ramey, but Had not got a chance to go to Jeter - Pillars -- remember the Pillars in St. Louis?
At a club they worked so long, so many years.
And what was that, the Plantation?
That's it. That's it. And so Had not told me, he says, "Well, I know they offered me more money. I think what I should do is go down there and take that." So I says, "Well, everything's cool."
He had been working with Countess Johnson. You remember Countess Johnson?
Oh, yes. Well, I don't know her, but I know of her.
Of her, yes. And she had had a group there and --
Was she a good piano player?

Yes, she could play. When Mary Lou got sick, they sent for her to play in Mary's place. Yes, she could handle a job, you know. I didn't enjoy -- I enjoyed her playing, but I didn't think she could really outplay Mary.
No, well, there weren't many people that could.
Right, that's the way I felt.
What about -- did she sing, this Countess Johnson, or was she just a piano player? (Unintelligible)? Or did she do like Julia Lee?
I don't think she did much singing, if any. Yeah, very little, if any. But she was a good pianist. And so --
